name: The American Club Resort
positioning: Historic resort hotel in the village of Kohler, Wisconsin, built in 1918 as a dormitory for Kohler factory workers, with the Kohler Waters Spa and Whistling Straits golf a shuttle ride away
best_for: Golfers who want a base for Whistling Straits and Blackwolf Run
Spa-focused getaways built around the Kohler Waters Spa
Travelers drawn to a hotel with a long history

facts.text: The Kohler family built the building that houses The American Club in 1918, well before it was meant to be a resort.
The building originally served as a dormitory for the immigrant workers who came to work in the Kohler factory.
In 1981 Herb Kohler, grandson of company founder John Michael Kohler, reopened The American Club as a hotel.
The American Club is made up of a number of buildings spread through the town of Kohler, built by the Kohler family.
Kohler is an Olmsted Brothers-designed community.
Room interiors are weighty, with wooden sleigh beds, patterned taupe carpets and hefty window treatments.
The art in most spaces is Americana: oil paintings of horse-drawn carriages, landscapes and vintage black-and-white photos.
The Carriage House, a few steps from The American Club, gives guests staying there unlimited access to the Kohler Waters Spa.
The Whistling Straits and Blackwolf Run golf courses are a shuttle ride from The American Club.
The Whistling Straits courses were designed by Pete Dye.
The Immigrant offers two menus: a five-course chef's tasting or a prix fixe.
In-room dining at The American Club is full service, with breakfast, lunch, dinner, quick bites and beverages.

highlights.text: The Kohler Waters Spa spreads across three levels of the Carriage House, from the basement to the rooftop, and has a small pool with a waterfall that massages bathers' necks and shoulders.
In the signature hydrotherapy treatment, guests receive a minty scrub on a massage table while warm water from Kohler showerheads rains down for 50 minutes.
Whistling Straits' Straits and Irish courses have hosted four majors and the 43rd Ryder Cup.
River Wildlife, a shuttle ride away, is a 500-acre outdoor recreation area with walking trails, canoeing, fishing and a hunting lodge.
The Greenhouse, a stained-glass structure Herb Kohler found in Europe and brought back to the garden of The American Club, is now a garden cafe serving coffee drinks and pastries.

considerations.text: Spa access is restricted to overnight guests on weekends, and treatments can book up months in advance.
Both The American Club and the Carriage House have elevators, but The American Club has stairs separating most spaces; the Carriage House has a simpler floor plan.
The resort is spread out, and shuttles are essential for getting around its many spaces.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The American Club, Kohler
